summary: Trend Detective is an interactive tool for testing changes in NASA Earth science data. Using NASA POWER / MERRA-2 monthly temperature and rainfall for 1991–2025 at 40 locations, it visualizes what changed, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant. Of 80 site-variable tests, 34 have p < 0.05 and 30 survive a false-discovery-rate correction. We then audited an apparent relationship: rainfall and temperature trends had a Spearman correlation of −0.55 across 12 named sites, but only −0.05 across 28 systematic grid points. By showing both results, the tool helps users distinguish local findings from patterns that depend on which places were selected.
details:
Team aini: Daniel Huang, John Xie, and Gabriel Wu.

Trend Detective answers the challenge with an interactive map and time-series views of temperature and precipitation trends, statistical significance, effect size, and a sampling audit. It is built with Python (standard library), JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. Source: https://github.com/ihateSAS/trend-detective

DATA AND METHOD

Monthly NASA POWER point data (MERRA-2 reanalysis, community AG), parameters T2M and PRECTOTCORR, 1991–2025, cover 40 locations: 12 named places and 28 points on a fixed 20° land grid. Only complete years are included. Temperature is the annual mean; precipitation is the annual total. Two-sided Mann–Kendall tests use tie and continuity corrections. Sen’s slope estimates change. Benjamini–Hochberg correction at q = 0.05 addresses multiple testing: 34 of 80 tests have raw p < 0.05; 30 survive correction.

OUR SELF-AUDIT

Across the 12 named sites, rainfall and temperature trends had Spearman rho = −0.55. Across the 28 systematic grid points, rho = −0.05; across all 40 sites, rho = −0.19. The broader sample undermined our initial story. The tool exposes that difference so users can inspect how selection affects conclusions. It does not establish a planetary mechanism or causation.

EXAMPLES

Dhaka: temperature −0.23 °C/decade (p = 0.012), rainfall +24.7%/decade (p < 0.001). Athens: temperature +0.50 °C/decade (p < 0.001), rainfall +5.9%/decade (p = 0.211). Los Angeles rainfall: −4.5%/decade, p = 0.53; reported as no significant trend. Temperature change is shown in degrees, never as a Celsius percentage because Celsius has an arbitrary zero.

BENEFIT AND LIMITATIONS

Students and other users can distinguish a visible slope from statistically supported change and see how multiple comparisons and site selection affect interpretation. Reanalysis is a model constrained by observations, the 20° grid is coarse, 35 years can include multi-decade cycles, and rainfall and temperature in a reanalysis are not independent. Planned improvements include block-bootstrap slope intervals, seasonal decomposition, and a finer grid.

AI DISCLOSURE

The existing project documentation identifies DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Fast as assisting the analysis pipeline, ingest.py, web demo, and first drafts under team direction and review. All reported numbers are computed by code against NASA POWER data.

REFERENCES

NASA POWER monthly API; Natural Earth 1:110m country boundaries (public-domain land mask/map); Mann (1945), Kendall (1975), Sen (1968), Benjamini and Hochberg (1995).
